words.gloss: accomplishment (of remedy) of the mishaps of vomiting and purging

hindi: अब इसके बाद हम वमन और विरेचन की व्यापत्सिद्धि की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the accomplishment (siddhi) in the mishaps of vomiting and purging.
notes: siddhi in the chapter title is rendered literally as 'accomplishment'; the compound can also be read 'the successful treatment of mishaps in vomiting and purging'. Chapter-opening formula. vamana = therapeutic emesis, virecana = therapeutic purgation (standard technical terms); the translation keeps the literal 'vomiting' and 'purging'.

lines_deva: अतिक्षुधितेन मृदुकोष्ठेनाल्पश्लेष्मणा दुर्बमेन दुर्बलेन हीनमात्रमतितीक्ष्णमतिशीतमजीर्णे वा पीतं वमनमधो गच्छति
lines_iast: atikṣudhitena mṛdukoṣṭhenālpaśleṣmaṇā durbamena durbalena hīnamātramatitīkṣṇamatiśītamajīrṇe vā pītaṃ vamanamadho gacchati
hindi: जो अत्यन्त भूखा हो, मृदु कोष्ठ वाला हो, जिसमें श्लेष्मा थोड़ा हो, जिसे वमन कराना कठिन हो, या जो दुर्बल हो, अथवा औषध मात्रा में कम, अति तीक्ष्ण, अति शीत हो, या अजीर्ण में पिया गया हो, तो पिया हुआ वमन नीचे की ओर जाता है।
english: In one who is very hungry, soft in the bowel, with little phlegm, hard to make vomit, or weak; or if the vomiting-medicine is of deficient dose, very sharp, very cold, or is drunk in indigestion, the vomiting-medicine drunk goes downward.

text_flags.why: possible: b for v; 'hard to make vomit' fits the sense and the list of instrumentals

notes: Instrumentals are rendered 'in one who'. The reading of hīnamātra...ajīrṇe as a list of conditions of the medicine and the patient follows the plainest sense; ajīrṇe could also be 'in one with indigestion'.

hindi: वहाँ इच्छित की प्राप्ति नहीं होती और मल उभर आता है।
english: In that case what is desired is not attained, and the waste matter (mala) is stirred up.

words.gloss: by suitable (ones), by those in proper combination
with regard to dose, time and so on

hindi: उसे फिर शीघ्र उपयुक्त साधनों से स्नेहयुक्त करके मात्रा, काल आदि का ध्यान रखते हुए वमन कराए।
english: Having quickly made him unctuous again with suitable means, one should make him vomit, with regard to dose, time and so on.
notes: yaugikaiḥ is taken as 'by suitable (means)'; the noun to be supplied is not stated.

hindi: और पहले हुई भूल को स्मरण करते हुए व्यापद् के कारणों से बचे।
english: And, remembering the earlier error, one should avoid the causes of mishap.
notes: OPEN (05.03.5) [minor] gloss / atikramam: Gloss 'transgression' vs translation 'error/भूल': 'error' is an interpretation. Suggested: earlier transgression / पहले का अतिक्रम

lines_deva: अजीर्णिनः श्लेष्मवतोऽत्युष्णतीक्ष्णलवणमात्रमहद्वं वा विरेचनमन्यद्वा भेषजमूर्ध्व प्रवर्त्तते

words.gloss: very hot, sharp, salty, or of great dose

hindi: अजीर्ण वाले और कफ वाले पुरुष में अति उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, लवण अथवा मात्रा में बहुत बड़ा विरेचन, या कोई अन्य औषध, ऊपर की ओर प्रवृत्त होता है।
english: In one with indigestion or one having phlegm, a purgative that is very hot, sharp, salty, or of great dose, or another medicine, goes upward.

text_flags.why: possible: garbled; 'greatness of dose' fits the list
possible: final m lost

notes: The printed spelling pravarttate (double t) is the edition's usual spelling of -vṛt-/-vart-; not flagged. The reading of mātramahadvaṃ is uncertain; the list could also be read without 'dose'.

hindi: वहाँ पहले कही गई व्यापद् और साधन।
english: There: the mishap as stated before, and the remedy (sādhana).
notes: Elliptical line with no verb. Read as vyāpat + sādhanam (two words); alternatively vyāpat-sādhanam as one compound 'mishap-remedy', with pūrvoktā agreeing with an unstated noun. Not resolved.

lines_deva: अतोऽप्यूर्ध्वमुत्तिष्ठति हृद्या बलेखनवट कवर्जमौषधं न तृतीयमवचारयेत्
lines_iast: ato'pyūrdhvamuttiṣṭhati hṛdyā balekhanavaṭa kavarjamauṣadhaṃ na tṛtīyamavacārayet

words.gloss: pleasant to the heart (first member of a compound continued in the next tokens)
scraping; vaṭaka (a small cake or pill)
words.gram: comp. members (ka stands in the next token)

hindi: इसके बाद भी वह ऊपर की ओर उठता है; हृद्य, अवलेखन और वटक को छोड़कर तीसरी औषध का प्रयोग न करे।
english: Even after this it rises upward; except for the hṛdya, avalekhana and vaṭaka, one should not apply a third medicine.

text_flags.why: possible: the words are wrongly divided in print (b for v, and ka separated from vaṭa); sense guessed as hṛdya-avalekhana-vaṭaka-varjam

notes: GLOSSARY OPEN: avacārayet rendered 'should apply' (plain literal). Subject of uttiṣṭhati is not stated. The reading of the compound is a guess from the damaged print; the meaning of hṛdya, avalekhana and vaṭaka as kinds of medicine is not stated in the line.

lines_deva: क्रूरकोष्ठस्यातितीक्ष्णाग्रे रल्पवीर्यं वा भेषजमुर्ध्वभागिकमधोभागिकं वा भक्तवदुपैति पाकं
lines_iast: krūrakoṣṭhasyātitīkṣṇāgre ralpavīryaṃ vā bheṣajamurdhvabhāgikamadhobhāgikaṃ vā bhaktavadupaiti pākaṃ

words.gloss: of very sharp fire (agni, the digestive fire)

hindi: कठोर कोष्ठ वाले और अत्यन्त तीक्ष्ण अग्नि वाले में, अथवा अल्प वीर्य वाली औषध ऊर्ध्वभाग से सम्बन्धित हो या अधोभाग से सम्बन्धित, भोजन के समान पाक को प्राप्त होती है।
english: In one with a hard bowel and very sharp fire (agni, the digestive fire), or if the medicine is of little potency, whether directed to the upper part or to the lower part, it undergoes digestion like food.

text_flags.why: possible: agneḥ/agner damaged, with r displaced to the next token
possible: spelling, ūrdhva with long ū

notes: The grouping of the vā-alternatives is uncertain (hard bowel and sharp fire together, or each separately).

lines_deva: तत्र समुदीर्णा दोषा यथाकालमनिर्ह्रियमाणा विभ्रमं कुर्वंति
lines_iast: tatra samudīrṇā doṣā yathākālamanirhriyamāṇā vibhramaṃ kurvaṃti

words.gram: m. nom. pl. pass. part. nir-√hṛ

hindi: वहाँ उभरे हुए दोष यथासमय बाहर न निकाले जाने पर विभ्रम उत्पन्न करते हैं।
english: There the aroused doṣas, if not expelled at the proper time, produce a disturbance (vibhrama).
notes: vibhrama: literally 'wandering about, confusion'; no specific condition is named in the line.

hindi: उस सुस्निग्ध कोष्ठ वाले को बहुत अन्न और औषध पिलाए।
english: One should make him, whose bowel is well unctuous, drink a plentiful amount of food and the medicine.
notes: The line literally has 'food' and 'medicine' as objects of the causative 'drink'. GLOSSARY OPEN: pāyayet rendered literally 'should cause to drink'.

lines_deva: कषायमल्पप्रत्ययं रूक्षं वा भेषजमस्निग्धस्विन्नेम वा पीतं शीतोपचारेण वा स्तब्धदोषं विग्रथितमयोगि भवति
lines_iast: kaṣāyamalpapratyayaṃ rūkṣaṃ vā bheṣajamasnigdhasvinnema vā pītaṃ śītopacāreṇa vā stabdhadoṣaṃ vigrathitamayogi bhavati

words.gloss: by one not oiled and not sweated

hindi: अल्प प्रत्यय वाला काढ़ा, या रूक्ष औषध, स्निग्ध और स्वेदित न किए हुए के द्वारा, अथवा शीत उपचार के साथ पिया जाए, तो वह स्तब्ध दोष वाला, गाँठ पड़ा हुआ अयोगि हो जाता है।
english: A decoction of little content (pratyaya), or a dry medicine, drunk by one not oiled and sweated, or with cold treatment, becomes ayogi, with the doṣas stiffened and clumped.

text_flags.why: typo: svinnema for the instrumental svinnena

notes:
GLOSSARY: kaṣāya = decoction (OPEN, kept as decoction; it can also mean the astringent taste). alpapratyaya and ayogi are doubtful in sense: pratyaya may be 'ingredient, basis'; ayogi is rendered literally 'not duly joined'. The subject of bhavati is not stated.
OPEN (05.03.12) [minor] english / not oiled and sweated: Ambiguous: asnigdha-svinna may be 'not oiled and not sweated' (gloss says so) but English reads 'not (oiled and sweated)'. Hindi has the same ambiguity. Suggested: by one not oiled and not sweated (if the gloss is right)

lines_deva: तत्र वमनेन भूयो वामयेद्विरेचनं स्निग्धस्विअस्य पुनर्विरेचयेदुत्क्लिष्टभूरिदोषं वा तृतीयेऽहनि
lines_iast: tatra vamanena bhūyo vāmayedvirecanaṃ snigdhasviasya punarvirecayedutkliṣṭabhūridoṣaṃ vā tṛtīye'hani

words.gloss: him whose doṣas are much agitated

hindi: वहाँ वमन से फिर वमन कराए; स्निग्ध और स्वेदित किए हुए को विरेचन से फिर विरेचन कराए; अथवा जिसके बहुत दोष उभरे हुए हों उसे तीसरे दिन।
english: In that case one should make him vomit again with vomiting; one who has been oiled and sweated one should purge again with purging; or one whose doṣas are much agitated, on the third day.

text_flags.why: typo: letters dropped

notes:
The clauses are elliptical; the division into three cases is the plainest reading. virecanam could also be 'the purgative'. 'Third day' is counted as stated, without further interpretation.
OPEN (05.03.13) [minor] english / with purging: virecanam is accusative, not instrumental: 'with purging' (also Hindi 'विरेचन से') is an import. Reading is elliptical; suggest 'as to purging'. Not patched: needs human choice. Suggested: as for purging, one oiled and sweated one should purge again

words.gloss: by lump (piṇḍa, probably bolus fomentation) and layer (prastara, fomentation on a heated spread bed); prastara is a standard named kind of sweating (sveda), piṇḍa probable

hindi: और दोनों संशोधनों में लवण और तैल से अभ्यक्त को पिण्ड स्वेद यानी सम्भवतः गरम पिण्ड से सेंक और प्रस्तर स्वेद यानी गरम बिछावन पर सेंक से स्वेदित कराए।
english: And in both purifications, one anointed with salt and oil should be made to sweat by lump (piṇḍa, probably bolus fomentation) and layer (prastara, fomentation on a heated spread bed).

text_flags.why: possible: should be one word by sandhi (tailābhyaktam); the space is a print error

notes: ubhayoḥ saṃśodhanayoḥ can be genitive ('of both') or locative ('in both'); 'in both' chosen. lavaṇataila is 'salt and oil' or 'salted oil'. prastara-sveda is a standard named kind of fomentation; piṇḍa is probably a bolus (lump) fomentation (probable, less securely attested); the line itself gives only the two words.

lines_deva: स्निग्धस्विन्नस्य च वमनमकृत्वा विरेचनं पीतवतः सामस्य वा मृदु वा विरिक्तस्याधोभागेऽत्यर्थगुरुस्तब्धोदरता शूलो वातपुरीषसंगश्च भवति
lines_iast: snigdhasvinnasya ca vamanamakṛtvā virecanaṃ pītavataḥ sāmasya vā mṛdu vā viriktasyādhobhāge'tyarthagurustabdhodaratā śūlo vātapurīṣasaṃgaśca bhavati

words.gloss: excessive heaviness and stiffness of the belly
piercing pain (śūla; colic in the belly)

hindi: स्निग्ध और स्वेदित किए हुए, वमन न कराकर विरेचन पीने वाले का, या आम सहित का, या मृदु विरेचन से विरिक्त का, नीचे के भाग में अत्यन्त भारीपन, पेट की कठोरता, शूल यानी तीव्र चुभने वाली पीड़ा, तथा वात और मल का अवरोध होता है।
english: In one who was oiled and sweated, and who drank a purgative without having been made to vomit, or one with raw (āma) matter, or one mildly purged, there occur in the lower part excessive heaviness and stiffness of the belly, piercing pain (śūla, colic), and obstruction of wind (vāta) and stool.
notes: The grouping of the genitives and of 'mṛdu vā' is the plainest reading; mṛdu may be read 'mildly' (with viriktasya) or as 'a mild (purgative)'. śūla: piercing pain, in this abdominal setting colic (standard).

lines_deva: तमप्ययोगिनं समूत्रैस्तीक्ष्णैरास्थाप्य जांगलरसैश्च भोजयित्वा फलदारुपिप्पलीसिद्धेन तैलेनानुवास्य वातहरैश्च स्नेहैरुपस्नेह्य पुनस्तीक्ष्णैर्विरेचयेत्
lines_iast: tamapyayoginaṃ samūtraistīkṣṇairāsthāpya jāṃgalarasaiśca bhojayitvā phaladārupippalīsiddhena tailenānuvāsya vātaharaiśca snehairupasnehya punastīkṣṇairvirecayet

words.gloss: having given āsthāpana (decoction enema, standard; literally 'making stand')
with juices/broths of jāṅgala (dry-land animals; standard: meat broths)
prepared with phala (disputed; perhaps madanaphala, Randia dumetorum), dāru (probable: devadāru, Cedrus deodara) and pippalī (long pepper, Piper longum; standard)
having given anuvāsana (oil enema, standard; literally 'making stay')

hindi: उस अयोगि को भी मूत्र सहित तीक्ष्ण द्रव्यों से आस्थापन यानी निरूह बस्ति करके, जाङ्गल रसों यानी सूखे देश के पशु-पक्षियों के मांसरस से भोजन कराकर, फल, दारु और पिप्पली यानी पीपर से सिद्ध तैल से अनुवासन यानी तैल-बस्ति करके, वात को हरने वाले स्नेहों से फिर स्निग्ध करके, पुनः तीक्ष्ण द्रव्यों से विरेचन कराए।
english: Having given even him, the ayogin one, āsthāpana (decoction enema) with sharp (substances) together with urine, having fed him with jāṅgala juices (meat broths of dry-land animals), having given anuvāsana (oil enema) with oil prepared with phala, dāru and pippalī (long pepper), and having made him further unctuous with Vāta-taking-away oils, one should purge him again with sharp (substances).
notes:
āsthāpana and anuvāsana are kept as the text's own words with a literal gloss; standard: āsthāpana = decoction enema, anuvāsana = oil enema (the line itself does not define them). 'Sharp (ones)' leaves the noun unstated, as in the Sanskrit. pippalī: standard; dāru: probable (devadāru); phala: disputed (madanaphala is one suggestion), the line does not say which. GLOSSARY OPEN: bhojayitvā 'having fed', virecayet 'should purge'.
OPEN (05.03.16) [minor] gram / tīkṣṇaiḥ (two occurrences): Genders n./m. are unfounded for an unstated noun and inconsistent. Not patchable (w occurs twice). Suggested: inst. pl. for both
OPEN (05.03.16) [minor] hindi / तीक्ष्ण द्रव्यों: 'द्रव्यों' adds a noun that the note says is unstated (also units 19, 36). English uses '(ones)'. Suggested: तीक्ष्णों से

lines_deva: कफोल्वणस्यातिस्निग्धस्य गुर कोष्ठस्य मंदाग्नेर्वा मृदुप्रणीत मौषधं भृशमुत्क्लिश्य दोषान् जाड्यतंद्रादौर्बल्यांगसादान् जनयति
lines_iast: kapholvaṇasyātisnigdhasya gura koṣṭhasya maṃdāgnervā mṛdupraṇīta mauṣadhaṃ bhṛśamutkliśya doṣān jāḍyataṃdrādaurbalyāṃgasādān janayati

words.gloss: dullness, drowsiness, weakness, sinking of the limbs

hindi: कफ की अधिकता वाले, अत्यन्त स्निग्ध, भारी कोष्ठ वाले, या मन्द अग्नि वाले को मृदु रूप से दी गई औषध दोषों को अत्यन्त उभारकर जड़ता, तन्द्रा, दुर्बलता और अंगों की शिथिलता उत्पन्न करती है।
english: For one with Kapha abundant, very unctuous, heavy in the bowel, or of slow fire (agni), a medicine mildly administered, having greatly agitated the doṣas, produces dullness, drowsiness, weakness and sinking of the limbs.

text_flags.why: possible: final vowel lost
possible: m wrongly moved to the next token

notes: jāḍya is glossed plainly as 'dullness'; aṅgasāda as 'sinking of the limbs'. 'Of the bowel' (koṣṭhasya) with guru is read as a bahuvrīhi 'heavy-bowelled'.

hindi: उसे शीघ्र खुरचे।
english: One should scrape that up quickly.
notes: What 'tat' refers to, and what is scraped up, is not stated; ullikhet is kept literal ('scrape up').

lines_deva: लंघितं च संधुक्षिताग्निं पुनः स्निग्धं तीक्ष्णोष्णैर्विशोधयेत्
lines_iast: laṃghitaṃ ca saṃdhukṣitāgniṃ punaḥ snigdhaṃ tīkṣṇoṣṇairviśodhayet
hindi: उपवास कराए हुए और जिसकी अग्नि प्रदीप्त हो गई हो, फिर स्निग्ध किए हुए को तीक्ष्ण और उष्ण द्रव्यों से शुद्ध करे।
english: One who has been made to fast (laṅghana), whose fire (agni) has been kindled, and who has again been made unctuous, one should purify with sharp and hot (ones).
notes: 'Sharp and hot (ones)': noun not stated. laṅghita is kept literal ('made to fast', laṅghana).

lines_deva: सशेषाध्माय च वातश्लेष्मवते रूक्षाय सोदावर्त्ताय मंदाग्नये वा शीतं रूक्षं वा दत्तमौषधं भृशमाध्मानं करोति
lines_iast: saśeṣādhmāya ca vātaśleṣmavate rūkṣāya sodāvarttāya maṃdāgnaye vā śītaṃ rūkṣaṃ vā dattamauṣadhaṃ bhṛśamādhmānaṃ karoti

words.gloss: for one with residue and bloating
for one having Vāta and phlegm

hindi: अवशेष और आध्मान वाले, वात और कफ वाले, रूक्ष, उदावर्त वाले, या मन्द अग्नि वाले को दी गई शीत अथवा रूक्ष औषध अत्यन्त आध्मान उत्पन्न करती है।
english: For one with residue and bloating, one with Vāta and phlegm, one dry, one with udāvarta (upward-turning), or one of slow fire (agni), a cold or dry medicine given produces great bloating (ādhmāna).

text_flags.why: possible: ādhmāna expected as in the same line; read as given, with ādhmāya for ādhmāna

notes: saśeṣādhmāya is uncertain: sa-śeṣa-ādhmāya 'with residue and bloating' is taken; 'saśeṣāya ādhmāya' is another division. Not resolved.

lines_deva: तत्र मलसंगात्समुन्नह्य दहत्युदरमंतःशूलं दृतिवत्पार्श्वयोरापूर्णता शिरःपृष्ठरुजा श्वासः पायुवस्तिनिस्तोदश्च भवति
lines_iast: tatra malasaṃgātsamunnahya dahatyudaramaṃtaḥśūlaṃ dṛtivatpārśvayorāpūrṇatā śiraḥpṛṣṭharujā śvāsaḥ pāyuvastinistodaśca bhavati

words.gloss: pricking in the anus and bladder

hindi: वहाँ मल के अवरोध से बँधकर पेट को जलाता है, और भीतर शूल, चमड़े की थैली के समान दोनों पार्श्वों में भरापन, सिर और पीठ में पीड़ा, श्वास यानी सम्भवतः साँस फूलना, तथा गुदा और मूत्राशय में चुभन होती है।
english: There, from obstruction of waste, having bound up, it burns the belly, and there occur inner piercing pain (śūla, colic), fullness of the two flanks like a leather bag, pain of the head and back, śvāsa (probably labored breathing, dyspnoea), and pricking in the anus and bladder.
notes: The subject of dahati is not stated. śvāsa: in lists of symptoms the standard sense is labored breathing, dyspnoea (probable here). basti is rendered 'bladder' here as a body part. Printed pāyuvasti: read basti (spelling variant); likewise vasti in line 05.03.22.

words.gloss: taking away udāvarta (reversed movement of Vāta with obstructed stool and flatus) and ānāha (distension with retention)
with the procedures of anointing (abhyaṅga, oil massage), sweating, wick (varti, medicated suppository), kindling, powder, and basti (medicated enema)

hindi: उदावर्त यानी वायु के उलटा चलने से मल और वायु का रुकना, और आनाह यानी पेट का फूलना और मल-वायु का रुकना, इन्हें हरने वाली अभ्यंग यानी तेल मालिश, स्वेद, वर्ति यानी औषधि की बत्ती, दीपन, चूर्ण और बस्ति यानी एनीमा की क्रियाओं से उसका उपचार करे।
english: One should treat him with the procedures of anointing (abhyaṅga, oil massage), sweating, wick (varti, medicated suppository), kindling, powder and basti (medicated enema), which take away udāvarta (reversed movement of Vāta, with obstructed stool and flatus) and ānāha (distension with retention).

text_flags.why: possible: the word is wrongly divided in print

notes: The relative clause 'taking away udāvarta and ānāha' is taken to qualify the whole list of procedures. udāvarta, ānāha, varti, basti: standard meanings as given in the glosses.

lines_deva: क्षामेणाल्पबलेन मृदुकोष्ठाग्निना रूक्षेण स्निग्धेन वा स्विन्नेन सामेन वा बलवदौषधमुपयुक्तं सपित्तमनिलं परिदूष्य परिकर्त्तिकामापादयति
lines_iast: kṣāmeṇālpabalena mṛdukoṣṭhāgninā rūkṣeṇa snigdhena vā svinnena sāmena vā balavadauṣadhamupayuktaṃ sapittamanilaṃ paridūṣya parikarttikāmāpādayati

words.gloss: with soft bowel (koṣṭha) and soft fire (agni)
parikartikā (cutting-around pain; scissoring pain in the lower belly and anus, standard term)

hindi: कृश, अल्प बल वाले, मृदु कोष्ठ और अग्नि वाले, रूक्ष, स्निग्ध, स्वेदित, अथवा आम सहित व्यक्ति द्वारा प्रयुक्त बलवान् औषध पित्त सहित वायु को दूषित करके परिकर्तिका यानी चारों ओर काटने वाली पीड़ा उत्पन्न करती है।
english: When a strong medicine is taken by one who is lean, of little strength, with soft bowel and soft fire, dry or oiled, sweated or with raw (āma) matter, it corrupts wind (anila) together with Pitta and brings about parikartikā (cutting-around pain, scissoring pain in the lower belly and anus).
notes: Instrumentals are read as 'taken by'. kṣāma is glossed 'lean' (alternatives: emaciated, wasted). The grouping of rūkṣa/snigdha/svinna/sāma is the plainest reading.

words.gloss: in the navel, bladder, anus and male organ

hindi: वहाँ नाभि, मूत्राशय, गुदा और मेढ्र में दाह सहित चारों ओर से काटना, वायु का अवरोध और विष्टम्भ यानी मल का रुकना।
english: There: in the navel, bladder, anus and male organ, cutting-around pain with burning, obstruction of wind (anila), and binding (viṣṭambha, retention with constipation).
notes: No verb is stated; 'occur' is not added. viṣṭambha: 'binding, obstruction', in practice constipation with distension (standard).

words.gloss: joined with black tila (sesame, Sesamum indicum; standard), madhuka (probable: liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra, the yaṣṭīmadhuka of line 05.03.27 [standard]) and honey (madhu)
with picchā-bastis (slimy enemas; basti = medicated enema)
should give āsthāpana (decoction enema; literally 'make stand')

hindi: उसे काले तिल, मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी और मधु से युक्त पिच्छा-बस्तियों से आस्थापन यानी निरूह बस्ति करे।
english: One should give him āsthāpana (decoction enema) with picchā-bastis (slimy enemas) joined with black tila (sesame), madhuka (probably liquorice) and honey.
notes: tila: sesame (standard); madhuka: probably liquorice (probable), not madhūka (mahua); 'black' is taken with tila. picchā ('slime, sliminess') is kept literal. 'Joined with' could govern only the last items; the plainest reading is taken.

words.gloss: with milk boiled with the milk-bearing trees (kṣīrivṛkṣa; standard group of milky-sap fig trees: nyagrodha, Ficus benghalensis; udumbara, F. racemosa; aśvattha, F. religiosa; plakṣa, F. lacor/virens; lists vary)

hindi: अथवा क्षीरिवृक्षों यानी सामान्यतः वट, गूलर, पीपल, पाकड़ आदि दूध वाले वृक्षों के साथ पकाए हुए दूध से।
english: Or with milk boiled with the milk-bearing trees (kṣīrivṛkṣa, the group of milky-sap trees, chiefly figs).
notes: Elliptical: continues the previous unit (no verb). kṣīrivṛkṣa: a standard group, usually nyagrodha, udumbara, aśvattha, plakṣa (probable members; lists differ); the line names none.

lines_deva: शीतांबुपरिषिक्तं चैनं पयसा भुक्तवंतं घृतमंडेन यष्टीमधुकतैलेनानुवासयेत्
lines_iast: śītāṃbupariṣiktaṃ cainaṃ payasā bhuktavaṃtaṃ ghṛtamaṃḍena yaṣṭīmadhukatailenānuvāsayet

words.gloss: with oil of yaṣṭīmadhuka (liquorice; standard, Latin name in line 05.03.25)
should give anuvāsana (oil enema; literally 'make stay')

hindi: और इसे शीतल जल से सींचकर, जिसने दूध के साथ भोजन किया हो, उसे घृतमण्ड और यष्टीमधुक यानी मुलेठी के तैल से अनुवासन यानी तैल-बस्ति करे।
english: And one should give him, sprinkled with cold water and having eaten with milk, anuvāsana (oil enema) with ghee-maṇḍa and with oil of yaṣṭīmadhuka (liquorice).
notes:
payasā bhuktavantam is read 'having eaten with milk'. ghṛtamaṇḍena and the yaṣṭīmadhuka oil are taken as two means ('and'), not as one; the Sanskrit has no 'and'. yaṣṭīmadhuka = liquorice (standard).
OPEN (05.03.27) [minor] english / and with oil: 'and' added between two instrumentals that have no ca; notes admit this. Prefer asyndeton or flag it. Suggested: with ghee-maṇḍa, with oil of yaṣṭīmadhuka

hindi: कृश के लिए मधुर और बृंहण, सब विधि इष्ट है। आम सहित में लंघन और दीपन, और हल्का, रूक्ष और उष्ण अन्न-पान।
english: For one who is lean, every procedure that is sweet and bulking is desired. In one with raw (āma) matter: fasting (laṅghana) and kindling (dīpana), and food and drink that is light, dry and hot.
notes:
line 05.03.28: bṛṃhaṇa is rendered 'bulking' (literally 'making grow'). The words 'sweet and bulking' are taken together as qualifying vidhi.
line 05.03.29: No verb is stated; the line is elliptical and continues the previous unit.

lines_deva: निरामीभूते ( मध्यबलोपचारइव वातातपाभ्यामिव पांशु भस्मावकिरणैरित्यादि ) वातानुरंधे लघुक्षाराम्लं वातेऽधिके दधि साम्लं दाडिमत्वचा युक्तं भोजने पाने च युंजीत
lines_iast: nirāmībhūte ( madhyabalopacāraiva vātātapābhyāmiva pāṃśu bhasmāvakiraṇairityādi ) vātānuraṃdhe laghukṣārāmlaṃ vāte'dhike dadhi sāmlaṃ dāḍimatvacā yuktaṃ bhojane pāne ca yuṃjīta

words.gloss: when become free of raw (āma) matter
with the rind of dāḍima (pomegranate, Punica granatum; standard)

hindi: आम से रहित हो जाने पर मध्यम बल के उपचारों के समान, वायु और धूप के समान, धूल और भस्म के बिखेरने से इत्यादि, वात के अनुरोध से भोजन और पान में हल्का, क्षारयुक्त और खट्टा प्रयुक्त करे; वात के अधिक होने पर खटाई सहित दही, दाडिम यानी अनार की त्वचा से युक्त, भोजन और पान में प्रयुक्त करे।
english: When one has become free of raw (āma) matter (as with treatments of middle strength, as by wind and sun, by scattering dust and ash, and so on), in accordance with Vāta one should employ in food and drink what is light, kṣāra and sour; when Vāta is in excess, curd together with sour, joined with the skin of dāḍima (pomegranate).

text_flags.why: possible: instrumental plural expected; r lost
possible: anurodha expected; 'anuraṃdha' is not a known word

notes:
The bracketed words look like an inserted note in the edition (the brackets are in the printed text); kept and translated. The two printed parts after 'vāte' are read as a locative absolute 'when Vāta is in excess'. The sentence is hard: the reading is tentative.
OPEN (05.03.30) [minor] gloss / laghu-kṣāra-amlam: 'alkaline' is a modern chemical term; kṣāra literally 'ash-derived substance'. Suggest keeping kṣāra. Suggested: light, kṣāra and sour

hindi: और दाडिम यानी अनार के रस सहित घृत पिए।
english: And one should drink ghee (sarpis) together with dāḍima (pomegranate) juice.
notes: The 'ca' stands after sadāḍimarasaṃ in the printed order; the plainest reading is taken.

words.gloss: paste of tila (sesame) and devadāru (deodar cedar; standard, Latin names in lines 05.03.25 and 05.03.16)

hindi: अथवा उष्ण जल से तिल और देवदारु यानी देवदार का कल्क।
english: Or, with hot water, a paste (kalka) of tila (sesame) and devadāru (deodar cedar).
notes: Elliptical (no verb); tila and devadāru: sesame and deodar cedar (standard).

lines_deva: क्रूरकोष्ठस्य बहुदोषस्याल्पमात्रगुणं मृदु स्निग्धं वा शोधनमवचारितमुत्क्लेश्य दोषान्न निर्हरत्यल्पाल्यं च पित्तकफसंसृष्टं परिस्रवति
lines_iast: krūrakoṣṭhasya bahudoṣasyālpamātraguṇaṃ mṛdu snigdhaṃ vā śodhanamavacāritamutkleśya doṣānna nirharatyalpālyaṃ ca pittakaphasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ parisravati

words.gloss: of one with a hard bowel (koṣṭha)

words.gram: n. nom. sg. p.p. caus. ava-√car

hindi: कठोर कोष्ठ वाले और बहुत दोष वाले में अल्प मात्रा और अल्प गुण वाला, मृदु या स्निग्ध, प्रयुक्त शोधन औषध दोषों को उभारकर बाहर नहीं निकालती; और थोड़ा-थोड़ा पित्त और कफ से मिला हुआ बह निकलता है।
english: In one with a hard bowel and many doṣas, a purifying medicine applied, of small dose and quality, mild or unctuous, having agitated the doṣas does not expel them; and, little by little, mixed with Pitta and Kapha, it flows out all round.

text_flags.why: possible: y for p; 'little by little' fits

notes: The subject of parisravati is not stated (the doṣas or the medicine). 'alpamātraguṇam' could also be read 'of small dose, without quality'. GLOSSARY: kvātha/kaṣāya not involved.

words.gloss: binding (viṣṭambha; constipation with distension), heaviness, drying (śoṣa), koṭha (wheals, urticaria-like eruption; probable), itching, paleness (pāṇḍutā; pallor), sinking of the limbs, piercing pain (śūla)

hindi: और विष्टम्भ यानी मल का रुकना, भारीपन, शोष, कोठ यानी सम्भवतः चकत्ते, खुजली, पाण्डुता यानी रंग का फीकापन, अंगों की शिथिलता और शूल यानी तीव्र चुभने वाली पीड़ा उत्पन्न करता है।
english: And it brings about binding (viṣṭambha, constipation with distension), heaviness, drying (śoṣa), koṭha (probably wheals, urticaria-like eruption), itching, paleness (pāṇḍutā, pallor), sinking of the limbs and piercing pain (śūla).
notes:
The subject (the medicine or the retained doṣas) is not stated. koṭha: wheals or urticaria-like eruption (probable).
OPEN (05.03.34) [minor] hindi / अंगों की शिथिलता: śithila means slack; aṅgasāda is 'sinking of the limbs'. Hindi sense differs slightly (also units 17). Suggested: अंगों का बैठना (suggest; human choice)

words.gloss: with decoctions of tiniśa (Ougeinia oojeinensis; standard), dhava (Anogeissus latifolia; standard), aśvakarṇa (probable: sal, Shorea robusta), palāśa (Butea monosperma, flame of the forest; standard) and valā (Sida cordifolia; standard)
should give āsthāpana (decoction enema; literally 'make stand')

hindi: उसे तिनिश यानी तिनस, धव यानी धौ, अश्वकर्ण यानी सम्भवतः साल, पलाश यानी ढाक और बला यानी खरेटी के निर्यूहों से, मधु मिलाकर, आस्थापन यानी निरूह बस्ति करे।
english: One should give him āsthāpana (decoction enema) with decoctions (niryūha) of tiniśa, dhava (axlewood), aśvakarṇa (probably sal), palāśa (flame of the forest) and valā (country mallow), joined with honey.
notes: GLOSSARY OPEN: niryūha is rendered 'decoction', the same as kaṣāya and kvātha so far. The five plants: tiniśa, dhava, palāśa, valā standard; aśvakarṇa probable.

hindi: और जिसका परिस्रव शान्त हो गया हो, उसे फिर और स्निग्ध करके तीक्ष्ण द्रव्यों से शुद्ध करे।
english: And one whose flowing out has subsided, having again been made further unctuous, one should purify with sharp (ones).
notes: The noun for 'sharp (ones)' is not stated.

words.gloss: kindling (ones) (split across two tokens in print)
āsavas, ariṣṭas (medicinal fermented drinks; standard) and so on

hindi: और शुद्ध हो जाने पर दीपन चूर्णों तथा आसव, अरिष्ट यानी औषधीय किण्वित पेय आदि का प्रयोग करे। जब औषध पिया हुआ व्यक्ति वेग को प्रेरित करता है अथवा रोकता है,
english: And when purified, one should employ kindling (dīpana) ones: powders, āsavas, ariṣṭas (medicinal fermented drinks) and so on. When one who has drunk the medicine sends forth the urge, or holds it back,

text_flags.why: possible: dīpanān is wrongly divided in print, and the ā of āsava is lost

notes:
line 05.03.37: Whether dīpanān qualifies only the powders or also the āsavas and ariṣṭas is not clear. āsava and ariṣṭa: medicinal fermented drinks (standard).
line 05.03.38: GROUPING: lines 05.03.38 and 05.03.39 are one sentence (yadā ... tadā); 38 is the 'when' clause. The urge (vega) is not specified in the line.

hindi: तब इसमें प्रवाहिका यानी पेचिश उत्पन्न होती है।
english: then pravāhikā (dysentery; literally a 'flowing forth') arises in him.
notes: GROUPING: completes line 05.03.38 (yadā ... tadā). Pravāhikā is kept as the text's name; its usual modern equivalent is dysentery (painful straining with passage of mucus and blood), tagged standard.

lines_deva: तस्यां सदाहशूलं सपिच्छं श्वेतं कृष्णं सरक्तं वा भृशं प्रवहमानः कफमुपविशति
lines_iast: tasyāṃ sadāhaśūlaṃ sapicchaṃ śvetaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ saraktaṃ vā bhṛśaṃ pravahamānaḥ kaphamupaviśati

words.gram: pres. part. pra-√vah, m. nom. sg.

hindi: उसमें रोगी अत्यन्त प्रवाहित होता हुआ दाह और शूल से युक्त, पिच्छ से युक्त, श्वेत, काला अथवा रक्त से युक्त कफ निकालता है।
english: In that, the patient, flowing forth violently, passes Kapha that is with burning and pain, with slime, white, black, or with blood.
notes: The adjectives (sadāhaśūlam ... saraktam) are taken as agreeing with kapham. upaviśati is literally 'sits down'; rendered 'passes' (Hindi 'निकालता है') as the idiomatic sense; the alternative is a looser 'sits and discharges'. The subject 'the patient' is supplied from context (the person of lines 05.03.38-39); pravahamānaḥ is a bare nominative participle. Context (pravāhikā, line 05.03.39): the Kapha passed, white or black or with blood and with slime, corresponds to mucus in the stool (probable); the translation keeps Kapha.

hindi: उसका परिस्रव की विधि से उपचार करे।
english: He should treat him by the procedure of parisrava (a flowing round, oozing).
notes: parisrava is kept as the text's term (literally 'flowing round, oozing'; not yet in the glossary, which fixes only praseka as 'flow, trickling'); the procedure it refers to is not stated in this line.

lines_deva: पीतौषधस्य भेषजोद्गारच्छर्द्यादीनां निग्रहाद्वातादयः कुपिता हृदयमुपाश्रित्य हृद्रहं घोरमावहंति
lines_iast: pītauṣadhasya bheṣajodgāracchardyādīnāṃ nigrahādvātādayaḥ kupitā hṛdayamupāśritya hṛdrahaṃ ghoramāvahaṃti

words.gloss: of one who has drunk medicine
of medicine, belching, vomiting and the like

hindi: औषध पिए हुए व्यक्ति में औषध, डकार, छर्दि यानी उल्टी आदि को रोकने से वात आदि कुपित होकर हृदय का आश्रय लेकर भयंकर हृद्ग्रह ले आते हैं।
english: In one who has drunk the medicine, from holding back the medicine, belching, vomiting and the like, Vāta and the others, agitated, resort to the heart and bring on a dreadful hṛdgraha (heart-seizure).

text_flags.why: the letter ga seems lost (Devanagari हृद्रहं also lacks it); hṛdgraha 'heart-seizure' is the expected word; possible

notes:
The first compound is taken as 'holding back of the medicine, belching, vomiting, etc.'; alternatively 'medicine' refers to the drunk medicine itself being held back. hṛdgraha is translated from the suggested reading. hṛdgraha (literally 'heart-seizing', graha = grasp) is the text's name for a dreadful heart affliction; no standard modern equivalent is established (unidentified), so none is imposed. Vāta and the others = the doṣas Vāta, Pitta, Kapha.
OPEN (05.03.42) [minor] text_flags / kupitā (src) vs kupitāḥ (w): Printed 'kupitā' before 'hṛdayam' lacks the visarga (a visarga before h stays; the same edition keeps visarga before k, p, etc.). lines_deva: ततः प्रधानमर्मोपतापाद्वेदनाभिरत्यर्थमातुरः पीड्यते मोहहिक्काकासलालापार्श्वशूल्युतो वेपथुमानष्टसंज्ञो दंतान्कटकटायत्युद्वृताक्षो जिव्हां खादयति
lines_iast: tataḥ pradhānamarmopatāpādvedanābhiratyarthamāturaḥ pīḍyate mohahikkākāsalālāpārśvaśūlyuto vepathumānaṣṭasaṃjño daṃtānkaṭakaṭāyatyudvṛtākṣo jivhāṃ khādayati

words.gloss: from affliction of the chief vital spot
joined with bewilderment, hikkā (hiccup), kāsa (cough), saliva, side-pain (pārśva-śūla)

hindi: तब प्रधान मर्म के उपताप से रोगी वेदनाओं से अत्यन्त पीड़ित होता है; मोह, हिक्का यानी हिचकी, कास यानी खाँसी, लाला और पार्श्वशूल से युक्त, काँपता हुआ, संज्ञाहीन, दाँतों को कटकटाता हुआ, चढ़ी हुई आँखों वाला होकर जीभ को काटता है।
english: Then, from the affliction of the chief vital spot (marma), the patient is tormented excessively by pains; joined with bewilderment, hikkā (hiccup), kāsa (cough), saliva and pain in the side, trembling, with lost consciousness, gnashing his teeth, with eyes turned up, he bites his tongue.

text_flags.why: one n lost: vepathumān + naṣṭa-saṃjñaḥ gives -mānnaṣṭa-; Devanagari वेपथुमानष्टसंज्ञो has the same loss; possible

notes:
khādayati is literally 'makes eat'; rendered 'bites' (Hindi 'काटता है'). lālā 'saliva' is read as a member of the compound before pārśva-śūla; the compound could be segmented differently (lālā-pārśva as one) but this is the plainest reading. hikkā = hiccup and kāsa = cough (standard); pārśva-śūla = pain in the side.
OPEN (05.03.43) [minor] text_flags / mohahikkākāsalālāpārśvaśūlyuto: Printed '-śūlyuto' lacks the a of śūla-yuto (śūla + yuta cannot give -śūlyuta). The split silently uses śūla-yutaḥ with no text_flag. Suggested: Add text_flag {src: mohahikkākāsalālāpārśvaśūlyuto, suggest: mohahikkākāsalālāpārśvaśūlayuto, why: 'a lost after śūl; possible'}.

lines_deva: तं हृदयापसरणमाहुस्तस्मै भिषक् शीघ्रममुह्यन्नभ्यंगपूर्व धान्यस्वेदेन परिस्वेद्य तीक्ष्णमवपीडं दद्यात्
lines_iast: taṃ hṛdayāpasaraṇamāhustasmai bhiṣak śīghramamuhyannabhyaṃgapūrva dhānyasvedena parisvedya tīkṣṇamavapīḍaṃ dadyāt

words.gram: pres. part. a-√muh, m. nom. sg.

hindi: इसे हृदयापसरण कहते हैं। उसे वैद्य मोहित न होता हुआ, शीघ्र अभ्यंग पहले करके, धान्य के स्वेद से स्वेदित करके, तीक्ष्ण अवपीड दे।
english: They call this hṛdayāpasaraṇa (heart-withdrawal). To him the physician, not being bewildered, should quickly give a sharp avapīḍa, after anointing first and having made him sweat with grain-sweating.

text_flags.why: final anusvāra apparently lost before dh- (Devanagari अभ्यंगपूर्व likewise); the adverb abhyaṅgapūrvam is expected; possible

notes: avapīḍa is kept as the text's term; literally 'pressing down, squeezing out'. dhānya-sveda is read as 'sweating with grains' (the sveda done with grain). Verb for āhuḥ is plural impersonal ('they call'). avapīḍa: in the classical texts avapīḍa is also a kind of nasal medication (nasya), the juice of pressed drugs squeezed into the nose; here, after anointing and sweating, a strong avapīḍa is probably that nasal form (probable, not stated in the line). hṛdayāpasaraṇa (heart-withdrawal) is the text's name for this condition; no modern equivalent is established (unidentified). dhānya-sveda = fomentation (sweating) with heated grains.

words.gloss: mixed with yaṣṭīmadhuka (liquorice root, Glycyrrhiza glabra; standard)
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, n. inst. sg. (agrees with taṃdula-aṃbunā)

hindi: यष्टीमधुक यानी मुलेठी से मिले हुए तण्डुल यानी चावल के जल से वमन।
english: Vomiting-treatment (vamana) with taṇḍula-water (rice-water) mixed with yaṣṭīmadhuka (liquorice).
notes: GROUPING: lines 05.03.45 and 05.03.46 are one statement ('vamana with ... or with pungents'); 45 is also elliptical (no verb) and continues the 'should give' of line 05.03.44. yaṣṭīmadhuka = liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra (standard); taṇḍula = husked rice grain (standard), and taṇḍula-water is usually understood as rice-washing water (probable). The alternative reading of miśreṇa as agreeing with vamana is unlikely.

hindi: अथवा कटुओं से, कफ की प्रधानता वाले के लिए।
english: Or with pungents, for one in whom Kapha predominates.

text_flags.why: an extra ra seems to have crept in (dittography); alternatives kaphottarasya / kaphottare cannot be excluded; possible

notes: GROUPING: continues line 05.03.45 (the vamana). The last word is garbled; the translation follows the suggested kaphottarāya 'for one with Kapha predominant'. kaṭu = pungent (taste); the noun it qualifies is not given.

lines_deva: ततो दोषशेषं पाचनीयैः पाचयेत् यथादोषोच्छ्रयं च बस्तीन् वितरेत्
lines_iast: tato doṣaśeṣaṃ pācanīyaiḥ pācayet yathādoṣocchrayaṃ ca bastīn vitaret
hindi: तब दोष के शेष को पाचनीय द्रव्यों से पकाए और दोष के उभार के अनुसार बस्तियाँ यानी एनिमा दे।
english: Then he should cause the remainder of the doṣa to be cooked with pācanīya substances, and should give bastis (enemas) according to the prominence of the doṣa.
notes: pācanīya = 'to be cooked/ripened', kept. basti is kept (literally 'bladder, vessel'). ucchraya = height, prominence.

lines_deva: अस्निग्धस्विन्नेनाब्रह्मचारिणा वेगविधारिणा मृदुकोष्ठेन सुकुमारेण वा रूक्षमौषधमतिमात्रं प्रयुक्तमतिविरेकाद्वायुं कोपयति
lines_iast: asnigdhasvinnenābrahmacāriṇā vegavidhāriṇā mṛdukoṣṭhena sukumāreṇa vā rūkṣamauṣadhamatimātraṃ prayuktamativirekādvāyuṃ kopayati

words.gloss: by one not oiled and sweated

words.gram: past part. pra-√yuj, n. nom. sg.

hindi: जिसका स्नेहन और स्वेदन नहीं हुआ, जो ब्रह्मचारी नहीं, जो वेगों को रोकता है, जिसका कोष्ठ मृदु है अथवा जो सुकुमार है, उसके द्वारा अत्यधिक प्रयुक्त रूक्ष औषध अतिविरेचन से वायु को कुपित करता है।
english: A dry medicine used in excess by one who is not oiled and sweated, not continent, who holds back urges, who has a soft koṣṭha, or who is delicate, agitates Vāyu (wind) through excessive purging.
notes: asnigdhasvinna is read as 'neither oiled nor sweated' (contrast line 05.03.52 snigdhasvinna); 'oiled but not sweated' is the alternative segmentation. The instrumentals are taken loosely with prayuktam ('used by/in the case of'). koṣṭha kept (belly/bowel interior). a-brahmacārin literally 'not following brahmacarya'.

lines_deva: तेन सर्वांगग्रहणी विशेषात्पार्श्वपृष्ठश्रोणीमन्मार्मसु शूलं मूर्च्छा भ्रमः कंपः स्तंभो निस्तोदो भेद उद्वेष्टनं संज्ञानाशश्च स्यात्
lines_iast: tena sarvāṃgagrahaṇī viśeṣātpārśvapṛṣṭhaśroṇīmanmārmasu śūlaṃ mūrcchā bhramaḥ kaṃpaḥ staṃbho nistodo bheda udveṣṭanaṃ saṃjñānāśaśca syāt

words.gloss: in the sides, back, hips, nape, vital spots

hindi: उससे सर्वांग का ग्रहण, और विशेषतः पार्श्व, पृष्ठ, श्रोणी, मन्या और मर्मों में शूल, मूर्च्छा, भ्रम, कम्प, स्तम्भ, निस्तोद, भेद, उद्वेष्टन और संज्ञा का नाश हो सकता है।
english: By that there may be a seizing of all the limbs, and especially in the sides, back, hips, nape and vital spots: pain, fainting, giddiness, trembling, stiffness, pricking, splitting, twisting, and loss of consciousness.

text_flags.why: 'manmārmasu' is not a word; manyā-marmasu 'nape and vital spots' is expected; possible
grahaṇī (f.) does not agree with the neuter/masculine list that follows; sarvāṅgagraha 'seizing of all limbs' or -grahaṇam is expected; possible

notes:
sarvāṅgagrahaṇī is unclear; read as a name for a seizing of all limbs, low certainty (grahaṇī is also a technical word). The locative compound is read as qualifying where the pain etc. occurs ('especially'). bheda and udveṣṭana are literal 'splitting' and 'twisting/wrapping'.
