The text_flag therefore changes the sense without the words row showing it (rule 6 asks for the corrected form in words). Translating a line of confidence 'low' as a firm reading is also overconfident: grahaṇī is a real word (f. 'that which seizes') and the printed clause may be read differently. Suggested: Human decision: either put the corrected form in `w` (sarva-aṃga-grahaḥ) and keep the flag, or keep grahaṇī and translate it literally ('the seizer of all limbs') with the emendation only in notes.

hindi: उसे अभ्यक्त करके, धान्यों से स्वेदित करके, यष्टीमधु यानी मुलेठी से पकाए हुए तेल से अनुवासन यानी स्नेहबस्ति दे।
english: Having anointed him and made him sweat with grains, he should give anuvāsana (unctuous enema) with oil cooked with yaṣṭīmadhu (liquorice).
notes: anuvāsayet is literally 'should cause to dwell along'; anuvāsana kept as the technical term. yaṣṭīmadhu = liquorice (see line 05.03.45, standard). Unqualified taila usually means sesame oil (probable; the line does not say). anuvāsana = an unctuous (oil or ghee) enema, standard. Unit 51 continues this sentence (food and drink).

hindi: और वात को हरने वाला अन्नपान।
english: And food and drink that takes away Vāta.
notes: GROUPING: elliptical; continues line 05.03.50 (an implied 'he should give'). hara is literally 'carrying off'.

lines_deva: स्निग्धस्विन्नस्यातिमृदुकोष्ठस्य क्षुधितस्य वा तीक्ष्णवेगमविभूरि वा प्रयुक्तमौषधं सर्वं निर्हृत्य मलं धातूनपि द्रवीकृत्य स्रावयेदतियोगि भवति
lines_iast: snigdhasvinnasyātimṛdukoṣṭhasya kṣudhitasya vā tīkṣṇavegamavibhūri vā prayuktamauṣadhaṃ sarvaṃ nirhṛtya malaṃ dhātūnapi dravīkṛtya srāvayedatiyogi bhavati

words.gloss: of one with very soft koṣṭha

words.gram: past part. pra-√yuj, n. nom. sg.

hindi: जो स्निग्ध और स्विन्न है, जिसका कोष्ठ अत्यन्त मृदु है अथवा जो भूखा है, उसके लिए प्रयुक्त तीक्ष्ण वेग वाला अथवा बहुत अधिक औषध सब मल को निकालकर और धातुओं को भी द्रवीभूत करके बहा दे; वह अतियोगी होता है।
english: In one who is oiled and sweated, of very soft koṣṭha, or hungry, a medicine used that is of sharp force or very abundant, having drawn out all the waste (mala) and even liquefied the dhātus (body tissues), would make them flow out; it becomes excessive in application (atiyogi).

text_flags.why: avi-bhūri has no sense; ati-bhūri 'very much' fits the context of excess (Devanagari the same letters); possible

notes: The Hindi 'तो' (if) is an interpretive link for the optative srāvayet; the Sanskrit simply states 'would cause to flow; it becomes atiyogi'. sarvam may qualify malam ('all waste') rather than the medicine; taken so.

lines_deva: तं शतधौतघृतेनाभ्यज्य कषायस्वादुशीतैः प्रदेहपरिषेकावगाहान्नपानैः शर्करामधुमद्भिश्च लेहैः स्तंभयेत्
lines_iast: taṃ śatadhautaghṛtenābhyajya kaṣāyasvāduśītaiḥ pradehapariṣekāvagāhānnapānaiḥ śarkarāmadhumadbhiśca lehaiḥ staṃbhayet

words.gloss: with ghṛta washed a hundred times
with astringent, sweet and cold things
as smearing, pouring, immersion, food and drink
with those containing sugar and honey

hindi: उसे सौ बार धोए हुए घृत से अभ्यक्त करके, कसैले, मीठे और शीतल द्रव्यों से, लेप, सेचन, अवगाहन, अन्न और पान के रूप में, और शर्करा तथा मधु वाले लेहों से स्तम्भित करे।
english: Having anointed him with ghṛta washed a hundred times, he should make him firm (stambhayet) with astringent, sweet and cold things, as smearing, pouring, immersion, food and drink, and with licked preparations (leha) containing sugar and honey.
notes:
kaṣāya is taken as the taste 'astringent' here (it stands in a taste-list with sweet and cold); glossary lists kaṣāya as 'decoction' so far (OPEN): not applied in this unit, flagged for the reviewer. stambhayet literally 'should make rigid/firm'; 'check, bring to a stop' is the alternative. leha = 'licked thing, linctus'.
OPEN (05.03.53) [minor] english / with astringent, sweet and cold things, as smearing, pouring, ...: 'Things' and 'as' are added. The instrumentals kaṣāya-svādu-śītaiḥ and pradeha-...-pānaiḥ are probably one phrase: astringent, sweet, cold smearings, pourings, immersions, foods and drinks. The word row also calls the first three a separate dvandva. Suggested: Human decision; suggested wording: 'with astringent, sweet and cold smearings, pourings, immersions, foods and drinks'.

words.gloss: aṃjana (disputed: a collyrium mineral such as stibnite/sauvīrāñjana, or a plant; unidentified here)
saktu (meal of parched grain, as in sattu)

hindi: चन्दन, अञ्जन, उशीर यानी खस, छाग यानी बकरे का रक्त, शीतल जल, एला यानी इलायची और लाज यानी खील के सक्तु यानी सत्तू पिलाए।
english: He should give to drink caṃdana (sandalwood), aṃjana, uśīra (vetiver root), goat's blood, cold water, elā (cardamom), and saktu meal of lāja (parched rice).
notes: One long dvandva; its segmentation into items is the plainest reading (chāga-asṛk 'goat's blood' as one item; lāja-saktu 'meal of parched grain' as one item). Alternative: all members are ingredients of one drink. Identifications: caṃdana Santalum album (standard); uśīra Chrysopogon zizanioides = Vetiveria zizanioides (standard); elā Elettaria cardamomum (probable; a larger cardamom, Amomum subulatum, is the alternative); lāja parched rice (standard); aṃjana disputed (a collyrium mineral such as stibnite, or a plant) and left unidentified.

hindi: और इसे पिच्छाबस्ति यानी चिपचिपा एनिमा दे।
english: And he should give him a picchā-basti (a basti of slime, i.e. a mucilaginous enema).
notes: picchā is read as 'slime, sliminess'; basti kept as the technical term. Contents not stated.

lines_deva: मधुरवर्गसिद्धं च क्षीरसर्पिः सर्पिर्मंडो वा ऽनुवासनं
hindi: मधुर वर्ग से सिद्ध क्षीरसर्पिस्, अथवा घृतमण्ड, अनुवासन यानी स्नेहबस्ति के रूप में।
english: Milk-ghee cooked with the sweet group, or the maṇḍa of ghee, as anuvāsana (unctuous enema).
notes: The construction is elliptical: madhuravargasiddhaṃ ca kṣīrasarpiḥ is read as one phrase 'milk-ghee cooked with the sweet group'; kṣīrasarpiḥ could instead be 'milk and ghee' (dvandva). maṇḍa kept (literally the clear upper part). 'madhura-varga' = the group of sweet things; not itemised.

hindi: और रक्तपित्त यानी रक्तस्राव के रोग की विधि करे।
english: And he should carry out the procedure for raktapitta (a bleeding disorder).
notes: raktapitta is kept as the text's term (literally 'blood-Pitta'). raktapitta = the classical bleeding disorder (haemorrhage from the body's openings, literally 'blood-Pitta'); standard.

lines_deva: विशेषेण तु वमनातियोगे सघृतसिताक्षौद्रं फलरसैर्मंथं पिबेत्
lines_iast: viśeṣeṇa tu vamanātiyoge saghṛtasitākṣaudraṃ phalarasairmaṃthaṃ pibet

words.gloss: with ghṛta (ghee), sitā (white sugar) and kṣaudra (honey)

hindi: विशेष रूप से वमन के अतियोग में घृत, सिता यानी मिश्री और क्षौद्र यानी शहद सहित, फलों के रसों के साथ मन्थ पीए।
english: But especially in excess application of vamana, he should drink a mantha (churned drink) with ghṛta (ghee), sitā (white sugar) and kṣaudra (honey), together with fruit juices.
notes: sitā read as 'white sugar', kṣaudra as 'honey' (both kept as terms). mantha is kept (literally a stirred/churned drink); its base is not stated.

lines_deva: क्षीरिवृक्षशुंगसिद्धां वा समाक्षिकां पेयां क्षीरं वा संग्राहिद्रव्यसिद्धं च क्षीरं भोजने चावचारयेत्
lines_iast: kṣīrivṛkṣaśuṃgasiddhāṃ vā samākṣikāṃ peyāṃ kṣīraṃ vā saṃgrāhidravyasiddhaṃ ca kṣīraṃ bhojane cāvacārayet

words.gloss: cooked with shoots of the milky trees (kṣīrivṛkṣa, the fig-family milky-sap trees)

hindi: क्षीरिवृक्षों यानी दूध वाले वृक्षों के अंकुरों से सिद्ध, माक्षिक सहित पेया, अथवा क्षीर, और संग्राही द्रव्यों से सिद्ध क्षीर भोजन में दे।
english: A thin gruel (peyā) cooked with shoots of the milky trees (kṣīrivṛkṣa), with mākṣika; or milk; and milk cooked with binding (saṃgrāhin) substances, he should administer at the meal.
notes:
Construction is loose: the verb avacārayet (glossary: OPEN, literal 'should administer') may govern the whole list, or only the final 'milk cooked with binding substances at the meal'; the translation follows the first reading (the verb governs the whole list). mākṣika may be 'honey' or a mineral name; kept as mākṣika. kṣīrivṛkṣa = the milky-sap trees, usually the four fig-family trees nyagrodha (Ficus benghalensis), udumbara (Ficus racemosa), aśvattha (Ficus religiosa) and plakṣa (Ficus lacor); probable, lists vary. mākṣika beside gruel is probably honey (probable; the same word is also a mineral name elsewhere); the translation keeps mākṣika.
OPEN (05.03.59) [minor] hindi / क्षीरिवृक्षों यानी दूध वाले वृक्षों: Hindi gives no ordinary names for the kṣīrivṛkṣa group although the notes name four trees (probable, lists vary); optional, left for the owner because the group membership varies. Suggested: optionally add 'बरगद, गूलर, पीपल, पाकड़ आदि' with a probable tag in notes

lines_deva: सोद्गारायां च छर्द्यां धनिकामधुकमधुरसमुस्तांजनानि मधुना लिह्यात्
lines_iast: sodgārāyāṃ ca chardyāṃ dhanikāmadhukamadhurasamustāṃjanāni madhunā lihyāt
hindi: और डकार सहित छर्दि यानी उल्टी में धनिका, मधुक यानी मुलेठी, मधुरस, मुस्ता यानी नागरमोथा और अञ्जन शहद के साथ चाटे।
english: And in vomiting with belching, he should lick dhanikā, madhuka (liquorice), madhurasa, mustā (nut-grass) and aṃjana with honey.
notes: The drug list is a dvandva; madhurasa could be read as 'sweet taste' but is kept as an item name. madhuka = liquorice (probable; spelled with short u, not the mahua tree madhūka); mustā = Cyperus rotundus (standard); dhanikā, madhurasa unidentified; aṃjana disputed (see line 05.03.54).

lines_deva: वाक्संगे हनुसंहनने ऽनिलार्त्तौ च घृतमांसरससिद्धामल्पतंडुलां पेयां पिबेत् स्नेहस्वेदौ चावचारयेत्
lines_iast: vāksaṃge hanusaṃhanane 'nilārttau ca ghṛtamāṃsarasasiddhāmalpataṃḍulāṃ peyāṃ pibet snehasvedau cāvacārayet

words.gloss: in closing of the jaws (lockjaw-like, trismus; probable)

hindi: वाणी के रुकने, हनु के जकड़ जाने और वायु की पीड़ा में घृत और मांसरस से सिद्ध, थोड़े तण्डुल यानी चावल वाली पेया पीए, और स्नेह तथा स्वेद का प्रयोग करे।
english: In obstruction of speech, closing of the jaws, and affliction by wind, he should drink a thin gruel (peyā) of few taṇḍula (rice) grains cooked with ghṛta and meat-broth, and should administer oiling and sweating.
notes: saṃhanana is literally 'compacting, close joining'. avacārayet: literal 'administer' used (glossary OPEN).

hindi: जीभ के भीतर चले जाने पर स्निग्ध, अम्ल और लवण कवलग्रह और गण्डूष, और हृद्य अज यानी बकरे के मांसरस।
english: When the tongue goes in: oily, sour and salty mouth-holdings (kavala and gaṇḍūṣa), and pleasing goat meat-broths.
notes: GROUPING: elliptical (no verb); it continues the 'should administer' of line 05.03.61. kavala-graha is read as 'holding a mouthful' and gaṇḍūṣa as 'mouthful'; whether they are two items or one is not clear. hṛdya literally 'of the heart', rendered 'pleasing'. kavala and gaṇḍūṣa are the two therapeutic mouth-holds (standard): gaṇḍūṣa is a mouth filled with liquid and held without moving, kavala a smaller quantity held and swished. aja = goat.

hindi: और इसके सामने खट्टे फल खिलाए।
english: And in front of him he should have sour fruits eaten.
notes: purataḥ may also be 'beforehand, first'; 'in front of' (plainest) taken.

lines_deva: निर्गतां जिव्हां तिलद्राक्षाकल्कलिप्तां व्योषलवणचूर्णप्रघृष्टां वा प्रवेशयेत्
lines_iast: nirgatāṃ jivhāṃ tiladrākṣākalkaliptāṃ vyoṣalavaṇacūrṇapraghṛṣṭāṃ vā praveśayet

words.gram: past part. nis-√gam, f. acc. sg.

words.gloss: smeared with a paste of tila (sesame, Sesamum indicum; standard) and drākṣā (grape or raisin, Vitis vinifera; standard)
rubbed with powder of vyoṣa (the triad dry ginger, long pepper, black pepper; standard) and salt

hindi: निकली हुई जीभ को तिल और द्राक्षा यानी अंगूर या मुनक्का के कल्क से लिप्त करके, अथवा व्योष यानी सोंठ, पिप्पली और काली मिर्च, तथा लवण के चूर्ण से घिसकर, भीतर प्रविष्ट कराए।
english: The tongue that has come out, smeared with a paste (kalka) of tila (sesame) and drākṣā (grape or raisin), or rubbed with powder of vyoṣa (dry ginger, long pepper and black pepper) and salt, he should make enter.
notes: tila = Sesamum indicum (standard); drākṣā = Vitis vinifera, grape/raisin (standard); vyoṣa is the group of three pungents śuṇṭhī (dry ginger, Zingiber officinale), pippalī (long pepper, Piper longum) and marica (black pepper, Piper nigrum), all standard.

words.gram: past part. vi-ā-√vṛt, n. acc. du.

words.gloss: sounds of sāman chant, flute, song

hindi: घृत से अभ्यक्त, पलटी हुई दोनों आँखों को दबाए। संज्ञाहीन को साम, वेणु और गीत के शब्द सुनाए।
english: He should press the two eyes, turned aside and anointed with ghṛta. To one who has lost consciousness he should make hear the sounds of sāman chant, flute and song.
notes:
line 05.03.65: vyāvṛtta is literally 'turned round/away' (rolled); the sense of which way is not stated.
line 05.03.66: sāma is read as sāman (chant); it could also be sāma 'gentle'. veṇu is read as 'flute'.

hindi: विरेचन के अतियोग में मिले हुए तण्डुल यानी चावल के जल से वमन करे।
english: In excess application of virecana (purgation), he should vomit with taṇḍula-water (rice-water), mixed.
notes: miśreṇa has no stated complement; compare line 05.03.45 (taṇḍula-water mixed with yaṣṭīmadhuka) — the text may drop the substance or the line may be incomplete.

lines_deva: प्रियंग्वादिकं च तंडुलोदकेन पिबेल्लोध्रसांजनदाडिमत्वचो वा कमलोत्पलसमंगापद्मकेसराणि वा
lines_iast: priyaṃgvādikaṃ ca taṃḍulodakena pibellodhrasāṃjanadāḍimatvaco vā kamalotpalasamaṃgāpadmakesarāṇi vā

words.gloss: the priyaṅgu group (priyaṅgu itself disputed: usually Callicarpa macrophylla)
skins of dāḍima (pomegranate rind, Punica granatum; standard)
samaṃgā (disputed: Mimosa pudica or Rubia cordifolia in different commentaries)

hindi: और प्रियङ्गु आदि को तण्डुल के जल के साथ पीए; अथवा लोध्र यानी लोध, अञ्जन सहित, और दाडिम यानी अनार की त्वचाएँ; अथवा कमल, उत्पल यानी नीलकमल, समङ्गा और पद्मकेसर यानी कमल के केसर।
english: And he should drink the priyaṅgu group with taṇḍula-water; or lodhra together with aṃjana, and the skins of dāḍima (pomegranate); or kamala (lotus), utpala (blue water lily), samaṅgā and padma-kesara (lotus filaments).
notes: GROUPING: lines 05.03.68 and 05.03.69 form one list of alternatives (vā ... vā ... vā). The scope of tvacaḥ is ambiguous: it may qualify lodhra as well (bark of lodhra, aṃjana and dāḍima). Identifications: lodhra Symplocos racemosa (standard); dāḍima Punica granatum (standard); kamala/padma Nelumbo nucifera (standard); utpala Nymphaea, e.g. N. nouchali (probable); priyaṅgu usually Callicarpa macrophylla (disputed); samaṅgā disputed (Mimosa pudica or Rubia cordifolia); aṃjana disputed (see line 05.03.54). priyaṅgvādika kept as 'the priyaṅgu group'; its members are not listed here.

words.gloss: skins of uduṃbara (cluster fig bark/rind; see line 05.03.59)

hindi: अथवा क्षौद्र यानी शहद, शर्करा यानी चीनी, मधुक यानी मुलेठी और उदुम्बर यानी गूलर की त्वचाएँ।
english: Or kṣaudra (honey), śarkarā (sugar), madhuka (liquorice) and the skins of uduṃbara (cluster fig).
notes: GROUPING: continues the list of alternatives of line 05.03.68 (verb pibet understood). Scope of tvacaḥ is ambiguous (it may govern madhuka and uduṃbara, or only uduṃbara). madhuka = liquorice is probable (as in units 45, 60), but if tvacaḥ governs it, the bark of the madhūka tree (mahua) is a possible alternative; uduṃbara = Ficus racemosa, cluster fig (standard); śarkarā = sugar, kṣaudra = honey (standard).

hindi: और रक्तातिसार यानी खूनी दस्त की क्रिया करे।
english: And he should carry out the procedure for raktātisāra (blood-atisāra, bloody diarrhoea).
notes: atisāra is kept as the text's term (literally 'excessive going/flowing'). atisāra = diarrhoea (standard); raktātisāra = diarrhoea with blood.

lines_deva: गुदं निःसृतमभ्यज्य स्वेदयित्वा कषायैश्च स्तंभयित्वा प्रवेशयेत्
lines_iast: gudaṃ niḥsṛtamabhyajya svedayitvā kaṣāyaiśca staṃbhayitvā praveśayet

words.gram: past part. nis-√sṛ, n. acc. sg.

hindi: निकले हुए गुद यानी मलाशय को अभ्यक्त करके, स्वेदित करके और कसैले द्रव्यों से स्तम्भित करके भीतर प्रविष्ट कराए।
english: Having anointed the protruded guda (rectum), made it sweat, and made it firm with astringent things, he should make it enter.
notes: kaṣāyaiḥ: 'astringent (things)' chosen; 'with decoctions' is the other possibility (glossary OPEN on kaṣāya/kvātha/niryūha). guda niḥsṛta (protruded rectum) corresponds to rectal prolapse (gudabhraṃśa); standard.

words.gloss: obstruction of speech and the rest

hindi: और पहले की तरह वाणी के रुकने आदि का साधन करे।
english: And as before, he should deal with obstruction of speech and the rest.
notes: sādhayet is literally 'should accomplish/bring about'; 'deal with' used.

lines_deva: उभयत्र च जीवरक्तपित्तयोर्ज्ञानार्थं रक्ते शुक्लं पिचुं प्लोनं वा क्षिपेत्
lines_iast: ubhayatra ca jīvaraktapittayorjñānārthaṃ rakte śuklaṃ picuṃ plonaṃ vā kṣipet
hindi: दोनों में जीवरक्त और रक्तपित्त को जानने के लिए रक्त में श्वेत पिचु अथवा प्लोत डाले।
english: In both cases, for the sake of knowing life-blood and raktapitta, he should put a white pichu (wad) or a piece of cloth (plota) into the blood.

text_flags.why: n for t; plota 'piece of cloth' fits 'white pichu or cloth' (Devanagari प्लोनं); possible

notes:
jīvaraktapittayoḥ is read as a dvandva of jīvarakta ('life-blood') and (rakta)pitta, matching raktapitta in line 05.03.74; the compound may have lost one rakta. ubhayatra 'in both' is presumably the two excesses (vamana and virecana) or the two blood-conditions treated above (raktapitta, raktātisāra); the text does not say. The translation as drafted reads the compound as jīvarakta + raktapitta (supposing haplology of rakta, cf. line 05.03.74); literally the printed compound is jīva-rakta-pitta, 'life-blood and pitta'.
OPEN (05.03.73) [error] english / life-blood and raktapitta (also Hindi जीवरक्त और रक्तपित्त; gloss '(rakta)pitta': The printed compound is jīva-rakta-pitta-yoḥ, literally 'of life-blood and pitta' (dual = two items). Both translations read it as 'life-blood and raktapitta', inserting rakta that is not in the text (an unflagged emendation, supported only by line 05.03.74). The gloss '(rakta)pitta' invents a bracketed member. This is a line of confidence 'low' yet it is translated as a firm reading, and there is no text_flag for the compound. Suggested: Translate literally ('life-blood and pitta' / 'जीवरक्त और पित्त') and put the haplology suggestion (jīvarakta-raktapitta, cf. line 05.03.74) in text_flags as 'possible'; the gloss should drop the bracket.

lines_deva: तस्मिञ्शोधाने कोष्णांबुक्षालितशुद्धे रक्तं वैवर्ण्ये तु रक्तपित्तं विद्यात्
lines_iast: tasmiñśodhāne koṣṇāṃbukṣālitaśuddhe raktaṃ vaivarṇye tu raktapittaṃ vidyāt

words.gloss: when clean after washing with warm water

hindi: उसमें शोधन होने पर, कुछ गरम जल से धोकर शुद्ध होने पर, रक्त को जाने; विवर्णता में तो रक्तपित्त यानी रक्तस्राव के रोग को जाने।
english: In that, on cleansing, when it is clean after washing with slightly warm water, he should know it to be blood; but in discolouration he should know raktapitta (the bleeding disorder).

text_flags.why: long ā looks like a scan slip; śodhane 'in the cleansing' expected; possible

notes: Elliptical: raktam and raktapittam are objects of vidyāt ('know (it as) blood / raktapitta'). koṣṇa literally 'slightly warm'.

lines_deva: अन्नं वा तद्विमिश्रं शुने काकाय वा दद्यात्
lines_iast: annaṃ vā tadvimiśraṃ śune kākāya vā dadyāt
hindi: अथवा उससे मिला हुआ अन्न कुत्ते या कौए को दे।
english: Or he should give food mixed with that to a dog or a crow.
notes: 'That' (tat) is presumably the blood under test in the preceding units; the line does not say so.

hindi: उसके खाए जाने पर जीव यानी जीवरक्त, और न खाए जाने पर पित्त।
english: When that is eaten, jīva (life-blood); when it is not eaten, pitta.
notes: Elliptical: the verb (something like 'one should know it as') is carried from earlier units and not supplied. jīva is read as jīvarakta ('life-blood') of the preceding units; pitta presumably stands for raktapitta as in lines 05.03.73-74; the line itself does not say so.

lines_deva: आमरणाच्च तस्य तृण्मूर्च्छामदार्त्तस्य क्रियां पित्तघ्नीमतियोगोक्तं च कुर्यात्
lines_iast: āmaraṇācca tasya tṛṇmūrcchāmadārttasya kriyāṃ pittaghnīmatiyogoktaṃ ca kuryāt

words.gloss: afflicted by thirst, fainting and intoxication

hindi: और मरण तक भी, प्यास, मूर्च्छा और मद से पीड़ित उसके लिए पित्त को नष्ट करने वाली क्रिया करे, और अतियोग में कहे हुए को भी करे।
english: And up to death, for him afflicted by thirst, fainting and intoxication (mada), he should carry out the Pitta-destroying treatment and what is stated for excess (atiyoga).
notes: āmaraṇāt is literally 'up to death'; whether it means 'as long as danger of death lasts' is not stated. atiyogokta is read as 'what is stated for atiyoga (excess)'; the noun is unstated. Printed 'ārtta' normalised to ārta; 'tṛṇ-' is tṛṭ (thirst) before m.

words.gloss: blood of khaḍga (probably the rhinoceros) and the rest
by the method stated for excessive flow (atisruta)

hindi: और खड्ग यानी सम्भवतः गैंडे आदि का रक्त, अतिस्राव में कही गई विधि से, मधु सहित, शीघ्र ग्रहण करे।
english: And he should quickly take the blood of khaḍga (probably the rhinoceros) and the rest, with honey, by the method stated for excessive flow (atisruta).

text_flags.why: the 'r' after 'sruta' is unexplained; atisruta + ukta is expected; possible (alternatively atisrute rakte-ukta, 'stated for excessive flow of blood')

notes: khaḍga = rhinoceros (probable; khaḍga also means 'sword'); 'blood of khaḍga and the rest' is as printed, the others are not named. What 'excessive flow' (atisruta) refers to is not stated here; the method is stated elsewhere (not in this unit). Read on the corrected form; the printed form is doubtful.

lines_deva: श्यामाकाश्मर्यदूर्वोशीरैर्वा शृतं पयो घृतमंडाजमयुक्तंशीतं बस्तौ निषेचयेत्
lines_iast: śyāmākāśmaryadūrvośīrairvā śṛtaṃ payo ghṛtamaṃḍājamayuktaṃśītaṃ bastau niṣecayet

words.gloss: with śyāmā (a plant; identity disputed), kāśmarya (Gmelina arborea, gmelina tree; standard), dūrvā (Cynodon dactylon, Bermuda grass; standard) and uśīra (Vetiveria zizanioides, vetiver root; standard)

hindi: अथवा श्यामा, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, काश्मर्य यानी गम्भारी, दूर्वा यानी दूब और उशीर यानी खस के साथ उबाला हुआ दूध, एक अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार बकरी के घृतमण्ड से युक्त, ठण्डा, बस्ति में डाले।
english: Or milk boiled with śyāmā (a plant of disputed identity), kāśmarya (gmelina tree), dūrvā (Bermuda grass) and uśīra (vetiver root), on a conjectural reading joined with goat's ghee-maṇḍa, cool, he should pour into the basti (enema).

text_flags.why: words run together and the middle 'ājamayuktam' is unclear (extra a before yukta?); conjectural, possible

notes:
The token 'ghṛtamaṃḍājamayuktaṃśītaṃ' is run together and doubtful; the printed middle part is kept unsplit (unclear) and the translation reads it, conjecturally, as 'joined with goat's (ājam) ghee-maṇḍa' (ghṛtamaṇḍa = literal 'ghee-maṇḍa', see glossary). śyāmākāśmarya is read as śyāmā + kāśmarya (śyāmā disputed: Operculina turpethum and Ichnocarpus frutescens are among proposals); kāśmarya, dūrvā, uśīra are standard identifications. niṣecayet is literally 'should pour/instil'.
OPEN (05.03.79) [minor] english / joined with goat's ghee-maṇḍa: Damaged token: only 'ghṛtamaṃḍa' and the final 'yuktaṃ' are reasonably clear; 'goat's' (from 'ājam') and 'joined with' are conjecture stacked on an unclear stretch, and ājam + ghṛtamaṇḍa is an odd pairing (ājya/ghṛta alternatives are possible). Draft does say 'on a conjectural reading' and gives low confidence, which is right; the owner may prefer to drop 'goat's' or keep the whole phrase marked as unclear. Suggested: Human decision: keep as drafted, or render as 'on a conjectural reading joined with ghee-maṇḍa'.

lines_deva: शेषेष्वपि चा सम्यक्प्रयुक्तवमनविरेचनोपद्रवेषु यथामयं दोषानपेक्ष्य प्रतिकुर्याद्वस्तिव्यापत्तिसिद्धिं चेक्षेत
lines_iast: śeṣeṣvapi cā samyakprayuktavamanavirecanopadraveṣu yathāmayaṃ doṣānapekṣya pratikuryādvastivyāpattisiddhiṃ cekṣeta

words.gloss: in the complications of improperly administered emesis and purgation

hindi: और अनुचित रूप से प्रयुक्त वमन और विरेचन के शेष उपद्रवों में भी, रोग के अनुसार दोषों का विचार करके प्रतिकार करे, और बस्तिव्यापत्सिद्धि को देखे।
english: And in the remaining complications (upadrava) too, of emesis and purgation improperly administered, he should counter them according to the disease, having regard to the doṣas, and should look to the basti-vyāpat-siddhi.

text_flags.why: ā is ca + the initial a of a-samyak (cāsamyak…); only the space is misplaced; possible

notes: 'cā samyak' is read as ca + a-samyak ('improperly administered'): the printed text without the space is cāsamyak, so only the spacing is off. The alternative ca + samyak ('properly administered') would need the printed ā to be an error. basti-vyāpat-siddhi presumably names the chapter of that name (cf. the colophon style); literally 'cure of the complications of basti'. Printed 'vasti' normalised to basti.

words.gram: loc. sg. (compound ubhayatobhāga, agreeing with śodhane)

hindi: इसी प्रकार दोनों भागों वाले शोधन में भी अवस्था के अनुसार उठ खड़ा हो।
english: Thus too, in cleansing through both portions (ubhayatobhāga), he should rise up according to the condition.
notes: ubhayatobhāga is probably cleansing by both the upper and lower ways (probable; the line does not say). uttiṣṭhet is literally 'should stand up'; the intended sense ('set to work, proceed') is not stated.

lines_deva: या तु विरेचने परिकर्त्तिका तद्वमने कंठक्षणनं यः परिस्रवः स कफप्रसेको यत्प्रवाहणं स शुष्कोद्गारइति
lines_iast: yā tu virecane parikarttikā tadvamane kaṃṭhakṣaṇanaṃ yaḥ parisravaḥ sa kaphapraseko yatpravāhaṇaṃ sa śuṣkodgāraiti
hindi: विरेचन में जो परिकर्तिका यानी काटने की पीड़ा है, वही वमन में कण्ठ की क्षति है; जो परिस्रव है, वह कफ का प्रसेक यानी बहना है; जो प्रवाहण है, वह शुष्क उद्गार यानी सूखी डकार है।
english: What is parikartikā (cutting pain) in purgation, that in emesis is injury of the throat (kaṇṭha-kṣaṇana); what is the discharge (parisrava), that is the flow of Kapha (kapha-praseka); what is straining (pravāhaṇa), that is dry belching (śuṣka-udgāra).

text_flags.why: missing space; hiatus, no sandhi, before iti (spacing only)

notes: Three equivalences between purgation and emesis; no verb is needed. kṣaṇana is literally 'hurting/wounding'; pravāhaṇa 'forcing down, straining' (cf. pravāhikā). Closing iti goes to notes only. Printed 'parikarttikā' normalised to parikartikā.

hindi: और इस विषय में ये हैं।
english: And on this point there are (the following).
notes: Lead-in formula introducing what follows; the thing that 'there are' (verses) is unstated, hence '(the following)'.

words.gram: past part. caus. a-√bhū, n. nom. sg.

hindi: अत्यधिक, अकाल में, थोड़ा, समान वीर्य यानी सामर्थ्य वालों से न भिगोया हुआ, भली-भाँति संस्कार न किया हुआ, पुराना, औषध निश्चय ही बिगड़ जाएगा।
english: Excessive, at the wrong time, scanty, not soaked (bhāvita) with (ones) of equal potency (vīrya), Improperly prepared, old, the medicine would surely go wrong (fail).
notes:
line 05.03.84: GROUPING: the sentence continues in the next unit, where the subject (the medicine) appears. bhāvita 'soaked' is the glossary rendering (steeped, impregnated); akāle may be 'out of season' as well as 'at the wrong time'.
line 05.03.85: GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in the previous unit (excess, wrong time, scanty, not soaked, improperly prepared, old: the medicine fails). jīrṇa 'old' follows the glossary; 'worn out, decayed' is possible. jīrṇa could also mean 'already digested' (the medicine digested without acting); 'old' kept per glossary (OPEN, owner).

lines_deva: छर्दनं न तु दुश्छर्द्ं दुर्विरेचं न रेचनं
पाययेदौषधं भूयस्तं निहंति तथा हि ते
lines_iast: chardanaṃ na tu duśchardṃ durvirecaṃ na recanaṃ
pāyayedauṣadhaṃ bhūyastaṃ nihaṃti tathā hi te
hindi: वमन नहीं, बल्कि एक अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार बुरा वमन; बुरा विरेचन, रेचन नहीं। औषध फिर पिलाए; वह उसे नष्ट करता है, क्योंकि वे वैसे ही हैं।
english: Not vomiting (chardana) but, on a conjectural reading, bad vomiting; bad purging (durvireca), not purging (recana). He should make (him) drink the medicine again; it destroys that (or him); for indeed they are so.

text_flags.why: damaged print: the vowel sign after 'rd' is missing; duś-chardaṃ ('bad vomiting') expected; possible

notes:
line 05.03.86: The printed word 'duśchardṃ' is damaged and kept unsplit; the translation reads it conjecturally as 'bad vomiting'. The line seems to say that a failed emetic becomes bad vomiting and a failed purgative bad purging, but this is a conjecture. chardana / recana could also mean 'emetic' / 'purgative' (the substance).
OPEN (05.03.86) [minor] confidence / duśchardṃ: Handling matches the glossary (unsplit, unclear, conjectural reading, low). Observation: the parallel 'durvirecam … recanam' suggests duś-chardanam rather than duścharda(m); the sense given is still conjecture. No change. Suggested: none
line 05.03.87: The syntax is unclear: taṃ may be 'him' (the patient) or 'that' (the remaining doṣa); the subject of nihanti and the referent of te ('they') are not given in this unit. Rendered as literally as possible; the sense is uncertain.
OPEN (05.03.87) [minor] translation / taṃ nihanti tathā hi te: Syntax unresolved, as the draft says: the subject of nihanti and the referent of te are unknown, and 'for indeed they are so' is a bare literal. Needs a human decision (low confidence is correct). Suggested: Human decision

lines_deva: वमितं केवलैः शुद्धं लंघितं पाययेत्तु तं
lines_iast: vamitaṃ kevalaiḥ śuddhaṃ laṃghitaṃ pāyayettu taṃ

words.gram: past part. caus. √laṅgh, m. acc. sg.

hindi: जिसके पीया हुआ, अनुलोमिक यानी स्वाभाविक दिशा में चलने वाला, कफ से मिला हुआ ऊपर की ओर जाता है, केवलों से वमन कराए गए, शुद्ध हुए और लंघन कराए गए उसे तो पिलाए।
english: In whom what is drunk, ānulomika (going in the natural direction), goes upward mixed with Kapha, But him who has been made to vomit with plain (ones), is cleansed and has been made to fast, he should make drink (it).
notes:
line 05.03.88: GROUPING: the sentence continues in the next unit. 'What is drunk' (pītam) is the medicine, unstated. ānulomika is literally 'going with the grain'; for a purgative this is probably downward (probable), but the line does not say. Syntax uncertain: ānulomikam may be adverbial ('goes in the natural way') or a noun, and 'goes upward' sits oddly with ānulomika for a purgative.
line 05.03.89: GROUPING: completes the sentence of the previous unit. kevalaiḥ 'by plain/alone (ones)': what is plain (e.g. unmixed emetics) is not stated. The object of pāyayet (the medicine) is unstated.

words.gram: past part. vi-√bandh, m. loc. sg.

hindi: दोष के रुके रहने, थोड़ा होने और देर से बहने पर गरम जल पिए। उससे आध्मान यानी अफारा, वमन, तृष्णा और विबन्ध यानी रुकावट शान्त हो जाते हैं।
english: When the doṣa is held back, scanty, and flowing after a long time, he should drink hot water. By that, distension (ādhmāna), vomiting, thirst and obstruction (vibandha) subside.
notes:
line 05.03.90: sravati is read as a locative participle agreeing with doṣe; it may also be 'it flows' (3 sg.). cirāt may be 'after a long time' or 'slowly'. The drinker (the patient) is unstated.
line 05.03.91: ādhmāna = abdominal distension, bloating (standard). The singular verb serves the whole list. 'That' (tena) is the hot water of the previous unit. vibandha = constipation / obstruction of stool and flatus (standard).

hindi: यदि दोष से रुकी हुई औषध न ऊपर जाती है और न नीचे, डकार या अंगों में शूल सहित होने पर वहाँ स्वेद का प्रयोग करे।
english: If the medicine, obstructed by a doṣa, proceeds neither upward nor downward, In that case, (if it is) with belching or with pain in the limbs, he should apply sweating (sveda).
notes:
line 05.03.92: GROUPING: the 'if' clause; the main clause is in the next unit. Printed 'pravarttate' normalised to pravartate.
line 05.03.93: GROUPING: completes the 'if' clause of the previous unit. The two adjectives are accusative neuter and presumably agree with an unstated noun (the medicine or the condition); '(if it is)' is supplied only for readability. avacārayet: glossary 'should apply' (OPEN).

words.gloss: (a person) properly purged, with belching; the medicine
when it does not set in motion

hindi: भली-भाँति विरेचित और डकार वाले की औषध को शीघ्र खुरचकर ऊपर निकाले। न पचे हुए और प्रवृत्त न होने पर वैद्य बहुत ठण्डों से रोके।
english: Of (a person) properly purged and with belching, the medicine he should quickly scrape up. But when (it is) undigested and does not set in motion, the physician should check (it) with very cold (ones).
notes:
line 05.03.94: The compound samyag-virikta-sodgāra-bheṣaja is read as 'properly purged, with belching, the medicine' with bheṣaja the object of ullikhet; this construction is uncertain. ullikhet is literally 'should scrape out/up'; the method is not stated.
line 05.03.95: The subject (the medicine) and what is checked are unstated. stambhayet is literally 'should make rigid, stop'. ajīrṇa taken as 'undigested'.

lines_deva: क्षीणे श्लेष्मणि सायान्हे रात्रौ वा तत्प्रवर्त्तते
lines_iast: kṣīṇe śleṣmaṇi sāyānhe rātrau vā tatpravarttate
hindi: कभी-कभी कफ से रुकी हुई औषध छाती में ठहरी रहती है। कफ के क्षीण होने पर, सायंकाल या रात्रि में, वह प्रवृत्त होता है।
english: Sometimes the medicine, obstructed by Kapha (śleṣman), stays in the chest. When Kapha has diminished, in the evening or at night, it moves on.

text_flags.why: letters transposed; sāyāhna is the standard form; possible

notes:
line 05.03.96: Printed 'kadācicchleṣmaṇā' is kadācit + śleṣmaṇā.
line 05.03.97: 'It' is the medicine of the previous unit (unstated). Printed 'pravarttate' normalised to pravartate.

hindi: जीर्ण यानी पचे हुए होने पर, ठहरे रहने पर, अथवा ऊपर गए हुए होने पर भी, रूक्ष अन्न खिलाए। किन्तु औषध के वायु से रुकने पर स्नेह और लवण सहित दूसरा पिए।
english: When (it is) digested, staying, or even gone upward, he should feed dry food. But when the medicine (is held) by Vāyu (wind), he should drink another (one), with fat (sneha) and salt.

text_flags.why: the accusative -m of rūkṣānnam appears lost (or rūkṣānnān); possible
sa-sneha expected; one 'sa' appears lost; possible

notes:
line 05.03.98: The syntax is uncertain: jīrṇe, tiṣṭhati and ūrdhvagate are read as three locatives (absolute) of an unstated subject (the medicine / Kapha). jīrṇa is rendered 'digested' here, not 'old' (the glossary rendering, used in an earlier unit for aged medicine), because the context is digestion; 'old' remains possible. tiṣṭhati may also be a verb ('it stays'). Metre: the printed half-line rūkṣānnāhārayejjīrṇe has 8 syllables; the suggested rūkṣānnamāhārayejjīrṇe would have 9, so the emendation is doubtful (printed form may be rūkṣānna + āhārayet).
OPEN (05.03.98) [minor] glossary / jīrṇe (digested) vs 85 (old): 'Digested' for jīrṇa/jīryati in 98, 100 (and ajīrṇa 'undigested' in 95) is correct for the digestion sense; the glossary entry jīrṇa 'old' only fits 85-type 'stale' use. Not an error in this chunk, but the glossary should state both senses; owner to confirm, and to decide 85 (old vs already digested). Suggested: Glossary: jīrṇa = 'old' (of a drug, stale) and 'digested' (jīrṇe, jīryati, ajīrṇa, of food/medicine in the body)
line 05.03.99: Elliptical: the participle (probably ruddha, 'held', carried from the earlier unit about Kapha) is not in the line. 'Another (one)' is a drink or medicine, unstated. sasnehalavaṇa could also mean 'salt with fat' (bahuvrīhi) instead of 'fat and salt'. Alternative to the suggested sasneha: the printed 'saneha' may be snehalavaṇam with a stray a, giving 'another one: fat and salt'; sense differs slightly.

lines_deva: पित्तघ्नं स्वादुशीतं च भेषजं तत्र शस्यते
lines_iast: pittaghnaṃ svāduśītaṃ ca bheṣajaṃ tatra śasyate

words.gloss: thirst, delusion, giddiness, fainting and the rest

hindi: प्यास, मोह, भ्रम, मूर्च्छा आदि हो सकते हैं, और औषध के पचते समय। वहाँ पित्त को नष्ट करने वाली, मीठी और ठण्डी औषध प्रशस्त है।
english: Thirst, delusion, giddiness, fainting and the rest may occur, and while the medicine is being digested. In that case a medicine that is Pitta-destroying, sweet and cool is recommended.

text_flags.why: tṛṇa ('grass') is not apt; tṛṇ- (tṛṭ, 'thirst') as in the earlier 'tṛṇmūrcchā' is expected; possible

notes:
line 05.03.100: The last clause is as printed: 'and while the medicine is being digested' qualifies the occurrence of the listed signs. jīryati may be read 'is digested / ages' (see glossary jīrṇa).
OPEN (05.03.100) [minor] glossary / jīryati: Rendered 'while being digested'; see 98 note. English 'and while the medicine is being digested' is a bare fragment of ca + locative absolute; literal, acceptable. Suggested: none
line 05.03.101: svādu 'sweet' may also be 'pleasant-tasting'.

words.gloss: from salivation, nausea, obstruction and horripilation (hair standing on end)

hindi: लालास्राव, हृल्लास यानी मिचली, विष्टम्भ और रोमहर्ष यानी रोंगटे खड़े होने के कारण कफ से ढके होने पर, वहाँ तीक्ष्ण और उष्ण, कटु आदि, कफ को हटाने वाली, हितकर औषध।
english: From salivation, nausea (hṛllāsa), obstruction (viṣṭambha) and horripilation (hair standing on end), when (it is) enveloped by Kapha, In that case, the medicine that is sharp and hot, pungent and the rest, Kapha-dispelling, beneficial.

text_flags.why: hallāsa may be a variant spelling of hṛllāsa ('nausea'); the standard form is hṛllāsa; possible
kad- is not a stem; kaṭu-ādi expected; possible

notes:
line 05.03.102: GROUPING: the sentence continues in the next unit ('in that case ... the medicine'). The ablative is read as marking the signs from which the Kapha covering is known; the subject (the medicine) is unstated. hṛllāsa = nausea (standard); viṣṭambha = obstruction, stiffness, binding (here as printed).
line 05.03.103: GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in the previous unit. Nominal sentence, no verb supplied. kaṭvādi could also name a drug group beginning with kaṭu (unclear).

hindi: गुदा की विपरीत गति, ग्रथितत्व यानी गाँठदार होना, भारीपन सहित। दोष का उत्क्लेश, अत्यधिक आध्मान, परिकर्त यानी काटने की पीड़ा, परिस्रव यानी बहना।
english: Contrary movement of the anus, knottedness (grathitatva), with heaviness. Stirring up of the doṣa (utkleśa), severe distension (ādhmāna), cutting pain (parikarta), discharge (parisrava).
notes:
line 05.03.104: A list of signs or complications; no verb. pāyoḥ is taken with gatiḥ; what is 'knotted' is not stated.
line 05.03.105: Continues the list of the previous unit. Printed 'parikarttaḥ' normalised to parikartaḥ.

words.gloss: pravāhikā (straining with frequent loose stools; roughly dysentery; probable)
with the flow of all the dhātus

hindi: प्रवाहिका यानी सम्भवतः पेचिश, हृदय का ग्रहण, और सारे अंगों का जकड़ जाना। सर्वधातुस्रव के साथ ये बारह उपचारों सहित कही गई हैं।
english: Pravāhikā (probably dysentery), seizing of the heart (hṛdgrahaṇa), gripping of the whole body. With the flow of all the dhātus, these twelve are stated, with their remedies.
notes:
line 05.03.106: pravāhikā = dysentery with straining (probable). hṛd can be 'heart' or 'chest'. Continues the list.
line 05.03.107: The instrumental is read 'together with' (the flow of all dhātus counted in the twelve); the text does not itself list the twelve here. The word 'etā' is etāḥ with the visarga lost before d.

words.gloss: from a lapse in the application (yoga)

hindi: योग यानी प्रयोग के भ्रंश से व्यापदें, विविध विरेचन में भी,
english: Complications (vyāpad) from a lapse in the application (yoga), even in purgation of various kinds,
notes:
GROUPING: this and the next two units form one sentence (continued in 109 and 110); no verb here. yoga may also mean 'combination (of the drug)'; vibhraṃśa 'slip, failure'.
OPEN (05.03.108) [minor] split / vi-vidhe: Possible variant dvi-vidhe ('twofold', i.e. upward and downward virecana, cf. line 05.03.81 ubhayatobhāga); printed vividhe is kept and is acceptable. Observation only. Suggested: none

lines_deva: उत्पद्यमानासु च तासु तासु व्यापत्सु संशोधनविभ्रमेण
दिशा ऽनयैवाशु यतेत सिद्धौ ज्योतिर्हि शास्त्रं नयदुर्नयानां
lines_iast: utpadyamānāsu ca tāsu tāsu vyāpatsu saṃśodhanavibhrameṇa
diśā 'nayaivāśu yateta siddhau jyotirhi śāstraṃ nayadurnayānāṃ

words.gram: pres. part. pass. ud-√pad, f. loc. pl.

hindi: और संशोधन के विभ्रम से उत्पन्न होती हुई उन-उन व्यापदों में, इसी निर्देश से शीघ्र सिद्धि के लिए प्रयत्न करे; क्योंकि शास्त्र नय और दुर्नय का प्रकाश है।
english: And in those various complications that are arising through a deviation in cleansing (saṃśodhana), By this very direction he should quickly strive for the cure (siddhi); for the śāstra is the light of sound and unsound conduct (naya, durnaya).
notes:
line 05.03.109: GROUPING: part of the sentence that is completed in the next unit. tāsu tāsu 'in those and those', i.e. in each of those.
line 05.03.110: GROUPING: completes the sentence of the two previous units. Printed "'nayaivāśu" is anayā eva āśu (the avagraha stands for the initial a). naya 'right policy/method', durnaya 'wrong policy'; siddhi 'accomplishment, cure'.

words.gloss: Vamana-virecana-vyāpat-siddhi (cure of the complications of emesis and purgation)

hindi: इस प्रकार वमन-विरेचन-व्यापत्सिद्धि नामक तृतीय अध्याय।
english: Thus the third chapter, named Vamana-virecana-vyāpat-siddhi (the cure of the complications of emesis and purgation).
notes: Colophon. The opening || is a printed mark. The title is read as vamana-virecana-vyāpat-siddhi 'cure (siddhi) of the complications (vyāpad) of emesis and purgation'. Closing iti belongs to the colophon formula.
